interpretation.interpretation: The diagram is a circular figure made of interlaced arcs in red, yellow and gray. A multicolored outer ring and a concentric inner ring are crossed by large arcs and short connecting arcs arranged with fourfold symmetry (top, bottom, left, right). It may be a schematic cosmological or elemental scheme, in which the colors and the fourfold arrangement stand for four parts, such as elements, qualities, winds or seasons. It may also be a purely ornamental or geometric interlace. The only text is the cropped red word at the lower left, tentatively read 'oecxelo' in Step 1. It lies outside the figure and is probably part of the surrounding text, so it gives no reliable key. No specific meaning can be assigned with confidence.
interpretation.evidence: The interpretation rests on visible features: concentric rings, a symmetrical arrangement of arcs in four directions, and the alternation of colors along the rings. The diagram has no internal labels. The free-standing text in Step 1 (entry 28) is cropped and uncertain, and it is not written inside any element, so it cannot support a textual reading. The Step 1 'above' relation between the outer circle and that text is also doubtful, because the text sits outside the diagram at the lower left. Some arc names in Step 1 are ambiguous because several arcs share similar descriptions and the interlacing is hard to follow. Entries such as 5, 8 and 26 to 27 have uncertain endpoints. Most Step 1 relations treat crossings as 'connected_to', which may overstate actual joins. No source or tradition is named, because none can be identified with confidence.
